title: Architecture Is the Verb: Three Timescales of Spectral Organization in Transformer Networks
summary: Transformer architectures are conventionally described by what they do on a given input. We show that the grouped-query attention (GQA) ratio, normalization scheme, and embedding configuration determine a processing verb -- tunnel, relay, or sort -- that persists through training, fine-tuning, alignment, and context variation. This verb is distributed across the architecture's collective geometry, cannot be localized to specific attention heads, and resists ablation. review.reason: Studies how transformer configuration shapes persistent spectral processing across training stages.
